title: Token Streamline Panel — microtraces, cohort lanes, and cost drift indicators
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design, prototype and spec a compact per-route / per-model 'Token Streamline Panel' for the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level microtraces, latency quantiles, throughput cohorts, and a cost-drift indicator. This ticket captures UX research, wireframes, high-fidelity prototype links, engineering handoff notes, and review feedback. Goal is a foldable panel that teams can add into route/model pages without overwhelming the primary dashboard.
design_goals: Show token throughput and latency distributions in a single compact strip for quick triage
Expose microtrace snippets on hover (first-byte, generation, KV-cache hits) for problem isolation
Surface cost drift and per-1k-token unit economics next to latency trends to inform trade-offs
Support cohort comparison (versions, regions, dedicated vs. hosted) with lightweight toggles
Keep visual noise low: single-line height, fold/expand behavior, and accessible color palette
chart_specs: Token Microtimeline (primary): horizontal stacked area representing token generation phases (prompt, kv-lookup, attention, decoding) with 8px height when collapsed; on expand shows full 48px height and p50/p90/p99 quantile ribbons overlaid as semi-transparent bands
Latency Sparkline with Drift Marker: small line chart (height 28px) showing moving window p50 and p95; vertical orange marker indicates >15% cost-per-token increase week-over-week
Throughput Lanes: 3-row compact bar lanes for 'hosted', 'dedicated', 'private' showing normalized TPS; hover reveals absolute TPS and sample count
Cohort Diff Toggle: when enabled, draws a thin overlaid delta ribbon showing divergence between selected cohorts (color-blind-friendly turquoise/magenta pair), supports up to 3 cohorts
KV Cache Hit Gauge: micro donut (24px) with tooltip listing hit %, sample time, and example key size distribution
Token Waterfall Detail (on-row drill): when a microtrace is clicked, open contextual panel with waterfall swimlane, token timestamps, and links to raw traces (sha256 id)
Cost Attribution Row: stacked bar showing compute vs. memory vs. infra rounding to cost-per-1k-tokens; includes toggle to show estimated savings for batch-size recommendations
research_notes: User interviews (n=8) with infra/platform engineers showed frequent need to correlate cost spikes with p95 latency increases at token boundaries
Design sprint test: collapsed view preferred by 6/8 for route list pages; expanded view used for incident postmortems
Accessibility check: default color ramp adjusted to meet 4.5:1 contrast for charts; added patterned fills for quantile ribbons to help colorblind users
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: microtrace fidelity vs. panel density — chose on-hover drill for full microtrace instead of always-visible detailed waterfall to preserve listing density
Decision: show p50+p95 by default, p99 available in expanded view to keep signal-to-noise high
Trade-off: cohort comparisons limited to 3 lanes to avoid clutter and binding performance cost in the frontend
Decision: use summarized KV cache hit % in compact view and link to detailed telemetry in Console's Trace Explorer
engineering_notes: Suggested telemetry: pre-aggregated quantiles (p50/p95/p99), token-phase durations, KV hit ratios per-route; windowed 1m/5m/1h buckets
Rendering guidance: canvas-based sparkline for performance; reserve 2 vector layers for quantile ribbons and cohort overlays
Data-size concern: avoid shipping full microtrace for all tokens — fetch detail on click via /traces/:id to reduce payload
reviews: 2025-02-20 - Priya Rao (PM): 'Love the compact form — ensure cost drift calc aligns with billing team's definition of unit cost', requested sample billing mapping
2025-02-22 - Mateo Alvarez (Engineering): 'Canvas approach OK; watch out for cohort overlay render cost on low-end machines', suggested debounce on cohort toggles
2025-02-25 - Security Review (note): 'No PII in traces; ensure trace ids are hashed'
2025-02-28 - UX Critique (team): 'Microtrace hover needs 200ms debounce to prevent flicker during pointer movement', agreed
usability_test_findings: Prototype run (n=12): median time-to-identify-root-cause reduced from 4.2m to 2.1m when using expanded Token Streamline Panel
Participants requested a keyboard shortcut to expand/collapse the panel for fast triage
Some confusion around cost-drift color semantics — changed legend to 'cost up'/'cost down' with arrows
accessibility_notes: All chart color pairs validated for Deutan and Protan using Coblis palette simulator
Quantile ribbons include patterned hatching for users who cannot distinguish hues
Panel supports full keyboard navigation: focusable lanes, drill-open via Enter, close via Esc
ARIA label example: 'Token Streamline Panel for route <route-name> showing latency and cost trends'
